tasks.title: Phase 1 – Project Bootstrap: CMakeLists.txt and AGENTS.md
tasks.description:
Initialize the C++ build system and fill AGENTS.md with all architecture decisions.

Files:
- CMakeLists.txt (new): find_package Qt6 (WebEngine WebEngineCore Network WebSockets), cmake_minimum_required(3.16), set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17), add_executable(anoa-browser), target_link_libraries with all Qt6 modules. Set Qt6 minimum to 6.4. Add Release strip flags (-s on Linux/macOS, /OPT:REF /OPT:ICF on Windows). Multi-arch: MSVC x64 /W4, GCC/Clang -Wall -Wextra. Define install(TARGETS) rule.
- AGENTS.md (update): Replace every TODO placeholder. File structure: src/browser/ src/http/ src/cdp/ src/pdf/ src/config/. Architecture decisions: Qt6/QWebEngine chosen, single binary, no Node.js, CDP via --remote-debugging-port passthrough (QTWEBENGINE_CHROMIUM_FLAGS), default port 9222. Naming: PascalCase for Qt QObject subclasses, camelCase methods, UPPER_SNAKE_CASE constants. Known gotchas: QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen for headless, Qt 6.4+ required, printToPdf is async (needs QEventLoop). Dependencies: Qt6>=6.4 with WebEngine/Network/WebSockets, CMake>=3.16, MSVC 2022 + Win SDK 10.0.22000 for Windows.

Acceptance criteria:
- CMakeLists.txt compiles a stub main.cpp that creates QApplication
- AGENTS.md has zero TODO placeholders remaining
- cmake --build succeeds on the target platform

tasks.title: Phase 8 – Config Module: CLI flag parsing and config file support
tasks.description:
Implement src/config/config.h and src/config/config.cpp for full CLI argument parsing and optional JSON/INI config file loading.

Files:
- src/config/config.h: Define struct Config { int port=9222; bool headless=false; bool noSandbox=false; QString profileDir; QString profileName; QStringList extensionPaths; QString authToken; }. Declare Config parseArgs(int argc, char* argv[]); Config loadConfigFile(const QString& path);
- src/config/config.cpp: Use QCommandLineParser. Flags: --port <port>, --headless, --no-sandbox, --profile-dir <dir>, --profile <name>, --extension <path> (addable multiple times), --auth-token <token>, --config <file>. If --config provided, load JSON (QJsonDocument) or INI (QSettings) and merge; CLI values always override file values. Validation: port must be 1-65535, exit(1) with message on error; warn to stderr if authToken is empty; each extensionPath must be an existing directory else exit(1).
- CMakeLists.txt: add src/config/config.cpp to target_sources.

Acceptance criteria:
- parseArgs correctly parses all documented flags including repeated --extension
- JSON config file is loaded and merged with defaults
- Port out of range exits with descriptive message and code 1

tasks.title: Phase 2 – Browser Core: QWebEngineView headless/headed mode with remote debugging
tasks.description:
Implement src/main.cpp (Qt entry point) and src/browser/anoa_browser.cpp/.h (QWebEngineView subclass) with headless/headed switching and remote debugging port activation.

Files:
- src/browser/anoa_browser.h: class AnoaBrowser : public QWebEngineView. Public: explicit AnoaBrowser(const Config& config, QWidget* parent=nullptr); void init(); Private: Config m_config; QWebEngineProfile* m_profile;
- src/browser/anoa_browser.cpp: In constructor body (before QWebEngine is initialized): set QTWEBENGINE_CHROMIUM_FLAGS env var to "--remote-debugging-port=<port>" + optional "--no-sandbox". If headless: set QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen. Create QWebEngineProfile: if profileDir+profileName set, use QWebEngineProfile(profileName, this) with storageName path under profileDir, otherwise use default profile. Set page to QWebEnginePage(m_profile, this). In init(): call show() only if not headless.
- src/main.cpp: int main(int argc, char* argv[]). Parse config first via parseArgs. Then QApplication app(argc, argv). Create AnoaBrowser browser(config). Call browser.init(). Start HttpServer and CdpProxy stubs (use forward declarations, wire up once those modules exist). Return app.exec().
- CMakeLists.txt: add src/browser/anoa_browser.cpp and src/main.cpp.

Key detail: QTWEBENGINE_CHROMIUM_FLAGS must be set via qputenv BEFORE QWebEngineView or QApplication is constructed with WebEngine initialization.

Acceptance criteria:
- Binary launches without crash in both --headless and visible modes
- Qt debug output shows remote debugging is active on the specified port
- profileDir creates isolated QWebEngineProfile storage

tasks.title: Phase 3 – HTTP Discovery Server: /json /json/version /json/list endpoints
tasks.description:
Implement src/http/http_server.cpp/.h as a QTcpServer-based HTTP server proxying Chromium-compatible CDP discovery endpoints.

Files:
- src/http/http_server.h: class HttpServer : public QObject. Constructor(quint16 port, quint16 debuggingPort, const QString& authToken, QObject* parent). bool start(); void stop(); private slot handleNewConnection(); private: QTcpServer* m_server; quint16 m_debugPort; QString m_authToken;
- src/http/http_server.cpp: On new connection, read HTTP request (until \r\n\r\n). Parse method, path, headers. Auth check: if m_authToken non-empty, require Authorization: Bearer <token> header or ?token= query param; return 401 JSON on failure. Routing: GET /json or /json/list or /json/version: create QNetworkAccessManager, GET http://127.0.0.1:<m_debugPort><path>, wait synchronously with QEventLoop, return proxied response body with Content-Type: application/json. Replace 127.0.0.1 in webSocketDebuggerUrl with the actual request Host header value. All other paths: 404 {"error":"not found"}. Cleanup socket after response.
- src/main.cpp: Instantiate HttpServer(config.port, config.port+1, config.authToken) and call start() after AnoaBrowser::init(). (debuggingPort = port+1 since Qt uses a separate internal debugging port; document this assumption.)
- CMakeLists.txt: add src/http/http_server.cpp.

Acceptance criteria:
- curl http://localhost:9222/json returns JSON array
- curl http://localhost:9222/json/version returns object with Browser, Protocol-Version, webSocketDebuggerUrl
- Unauthorized request returns 401 when auth token configured

tasks.title: Phase 4 – WebSocket CDP Proxy: session multiplexing and bearer token auth
tasks.description:
Implement src/cdp/cdp_proxy.cpp/.h as a QWebSocketServer-based proxy bridging external CDP clients to Qt's native DevTools WebSocket with per-session multiplexing and authentication.

Files:
- src/cdp/cdp_proxy.h: class CdpProxy : public QObject. Constructor(quint16 listenPort, quint16 debuggingPort, const QString& authToken, QObject* parent). bool start(); void stop(); Private slots: onNewConnection(), onClientMessage(const QString&), onClientDisconnected(), onUpstreamMessage(const QString&), onUpstreamDisconnected(). Private: QWebSocketServer* m_server; QMap<QWebSocket*, QWebSocket*> m_clientToUpstream; QMap<QWebSocket*, QWebSocket*> m_upstreamToClient; quint16 m_debugPort; QString m_authToken;
- src/cdp/cdp_proxy.cpp: In onNewConnection(): get pending connection, check auth (query param token= or header Authorization: Bearer). If invalid, send HTTP 401 close. Extract target path from socket->requestUrl().path() (e.g. /devtools/page/<id>). Open upstream QWebSocket to ws://127.0.0.1:<m_debugPort><path>. Store in both maps. Connect textMessageReceived on both sides. In onClientMessage(): call CdpExtensions::processCommand (inject after task-006; stub passthrough for now), forward to upstream if not handled. In onUpstreamMessage(): forward to client. On disconnect: close paired socket, remove from maps.
- src/main.cpp: Instantiate CdpProxy(config.port, config.port+1, config.authToken) and start().
- CMakeLists.txt: add src/cdp/cdp_proxy.cpp.

Acceptance criteria:
- WebSocket client connecting to ws://localhost:9222/devtools/page/<id> receives forwarded CDP messages
- Each connection creates exactly one upstream socket
- Connection with invalid token is rejected

tasks.title: Phase 5 – CDP Domain Extensions: Profiler, HeapProfiler, Security adapters
tasks.description:
Implement src/cdp/cdp_extensions.cpp/.h as a C++ adapter intercepting CDP messages for Profiler, HeapProfiler, and Security domains before they reach the upstream proxy.

Files:
- src/cdp/cdp_extensions.h: class CdpExtensions : public QObject. Static method: static QString processCommand(const QJsonObject& cmd, QWebEnginePage* page). Private static helpers: handleProfiler, handleHeapProfiler, handleSecurity.
- src/cdp/cdp_extensions.cpp: Parse method field (e.g. "Profiler.enable"). For domain "Profiler": enable/disable/start/stop/setSamplingInterval all return {"id":<id>,"result":{}}. For domain "HeapProfiler": enable/disable/startTrackingHeapObjects/stopTrackingHeapObjects/takeHeapSnapshot return {"id":<id>,"result":{}}. For domain "Security": enable/disable return {"id":<id>,"result":{}}; setIgnoreCertificateErrors: attempt QWebEngineProfile::setHttpAcceptLanguage (no direct API) and return stub result. For any unrecognized method in these three domains: return {"id":<id>,"result":{}} stub. For all other domains: return QString() (empty) to signal passthrough.
- src/cdp/cdp_proxy.cpp (modify): In onClientMessage, parse JSON, call CdpExtensions::processCommand; if non-empty result returned, send it back to client and return without forwarding upstream.
- CMakeLists.txt: add src/cdp/cdp_extensions.cpp.

Acceptance criteria:
- Profiler.enable returns {result:{}} without upstream forwarding
- Page.navigate passes through to upstream unmodified
- No crash on any Profiler/HeapProfiler/Security command

tasks.title: Phase 6 – Extension and Profile Management: loading, named profiles, cookie/storage CRUD

tasks.title: Phase 7 – PDF Generation: Page.printToPDF CDP command via QWebEnginePage::printToPdf
tasks.description:
Implement src/pdf/pdf_handler.cpp/.h to handle the Page.printToPDF CDP command using Qt's async printToPdf API bridged via QEventLoop.

Files:
- src/pdf/pdf_handler.h: class PdfHandler : public QObject. Constructor(QWebEnginePage* page, QObject* parent). QString handlePrintToPdf(const QJsonObject& cmd); Private: QWebEnginePage* m_page;
- src/pdf/pdf_handler.cpp: Extract params: landscape (bool), paperWidth/Height (double, inches, default letter 8.5x11), marginTop/Bottom/Left/Right (double, default 0.4in), printBackground (bool), scale (double). Build QPageLayout from paperWidth/Height (convert inches to mm via *25.4) and margins. Create QTemporaryFile and get filePath. Connect QWebEnginePage::pdfPrintingFinished(filePath, success) signal. Call m_page->printToPdf(filePath, layout). Run QEventLoop with QTimer::singleShot(30000) timeout that quits loop. After loop: if success, read file bytes, return {"id":<id>,"result":{"data":"<base64>"}}. If timeout or !success, return {"id":<id>,"error":{"code":-32000,"message":"PDF generation timed out or failed"}}.
- src/cdp/cdp_extensions.cpp (modify): Intercept method "Page.printToPDF": instantiate PdfHandler(page) and call handlePrintToPdf(cmd), return result. Add PdfHandler include.
- src/cdp/cdp_extensions.h: Add QWebEnginePage* parameter to processCommand or add setPdfPage(QWebEnginePage*) setter.
- CMakeLists.txt: add src/pdf/pdf_handler.cpp.

Acceptance criteria:
- Page.printToPDF returns {result:{data:"<base64>"}} with valid PDF (starts with %PDF-)
- Timeout after 30s returns error response without hanging
- landscape:true produces landscape-oriented PDF

tasks.title: Phase 9 – GitHub Actions Release Pipeline: multi-platform matrix build and GitHub Releases
tasks.description:
Create .github/workflows/release.yml for automated multi-platform binary builds triggered on version tag push.

File to create:
- .github/workflows/release.yml: Trigger: on.push.tags: ['v*.*.*']. Jobs:
  1. build-linux (runs-on: ubuntu-22.04, strategy.matrix.arch: [x86_64, arm64]): steps: checkout; cache Qt6 via actions/cache keyed by Qt version + arch; install Qt6 via aqtinstall (pip install aqtinstall && aqt install-qt linux desktop 6.6.0 gcc_64 -m qtwebengine); for arm64 install gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu and use toolchain file. cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release; cmake --build; strip anoa-browser; tar czf anoa-browser-linux-${{matrix.arch}}.tar.gz anoa-browser; upload-artifact.
  2. build-macos (runs-on: macos-13): cache + install Qt6 universal; build with -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES="x86_64;arm64"; strip; tar czf anoa-browser-macos-universal.tar.gz; upload-artifact.
  3. build-windows (runs-on: windows-2022): cache + install Qt6 MSVC 2022 x64 via aqtinstall; cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -A x64; cmake --build --config Release; 7z a anoa-browser-windows-x86_64.zip anoa-browser.exe; upload-artifact.
  4. release (needs: [build-linux, build-macos, build-windows]): download all artifacts; use softprops/action-gh-release@v1 with files: *.tar.gz, *.zip, generate_release_notes: true.

Acceptance criteria:
- YAML file is syntactically valid (no parse errors)
- Matrix covers all four platform/arch combinations
- Qt6 installation uses actions/cache to avoid re-downloading on every run
- Release job creates GitHub Release with all binary artifacts

tasks.title: Phase 10 – Integration Validation: Playwright/Puppeteer compatibility and protocol gap documentation
tasks.description:
Build the binary and validate end-to-end CDP compatibility against Playwright and Puppeteer. Document all findings.

Validation steps to execute:
1. cmake --build build --config Release (or cmake -B build && cmake --build build)
2. Launch: ./build/anoa-browser --headless --port 9222 --auth-token testtoken123
3. Playwright test: write a Node.js script (no package.json needed, use node --input-type=module): import {chromium} from '@playwright/test'; const browser = await chromium.connectOverCDP('http://localhost:9222', {headers:{Authorization:'Bearer testtoken123'}}); const page = await browser.newPage(); await page.goto('about:blank'); const title = await page.title(); console.log('Playwright OK:', title === ''); await browser.close();
4. Puppeteer test: fetch ws URL from /json/version, connect via puppeteer.connect({browserWSEndpoint: wsUrl}).
5. CDP domain tests via raw ws (use wscat or Node.js): Profiler.enable, HeapProfiler.enable, Security.enable, Security.setIgnoreCertificateErrors — verify no error codes in responses.
6. Page.printToPDF: send command, decode base64, verify first 4 bytes are 25 50 44 46 (%PDF).
7. Extension load: launch with --extension ./test-ext (create minimal manifest.json with manifest_version:2, name, version), verify no crash.
8. Profile isolation: two sequential launches with --profile profA and --profile profB, verify storage directories created.

For each step: document PASS/FAIL, error message if FAIL, and workaround.
Update AGENTS.md Known Gotchas with any new discoveries.
Update .jonggrang/progress.txt with full validation summary including CDP command coverage matrix.

Acceptance criteria:
- Playwright connectOverCDP succeeds without error
- All CDP domain stubs return valid JSON
- PDF has valid %PDF- header
- AGENTS.md documents known protocol gaps

tasks.title: Phase 1 – Config Extension: add width/height fields and --width/--height CLI flags
tasks.description:
Extend the Config struct with integer width and height fields (defaults 1280×720) and parse the corresponding CLI flags and config-file keys.

Files to modify:
- src/config/config.h: Add two new fields to the Config struct: `int width = 1280;` and `int height = 720;` placed after the existing fields.
- src/config/config.cpp: In parseArgs(), add two QCommandLineOption entries:
  - `QCommandLineOption widthOpt({"width"}, "Browser viewport/window width in pixels (default 1280)", "width");`
  - `QCommandLineOption heightOpt({"height"}, "Browser viewport/window height in pixels (default 720)", "height");`
  Register both options with parser.addOption(). After parser.process(), read them: if parser.isSet(widthOpt), convert to int with QString::toInt() and validate > 0; if invalid, print error and exit(1). Same for height. In loadConfigFile(), read "width" and "height" integer keys from the JSON object (QJsonObject["width"].toInt(1280)) and from the INI [QSettings] under keys "width" / "height". CLI values must always win over file values (apply file first, then overwrite with CLI values if parser.isSet()).

Acceptance criteria:
- `--width 1920 --height 1080` produces Config{width:1920, height:1080}
- Omitting both flags produces Config{width:1280, height:720}
- `--width 0` or `--width -1` exits with error code 1 and a descriptive message
- JSON config file `{"width": 800, "height": 600}` is loaded; CLI flag overrides file value

tasks.title: Phase 2 – Browser Core Wiring: apply width/height via resize() in AnoaBrowser
tasks.description:
Apply config.width and config.height to the QWebEngineView widget so both headed and headless modes render at the configured viewport dimensions.

File to modify:
- src/browser/anoa_browser.cpp: In AnoaBrowser::init() (or the constructor body, after m_page is set and before load() is called), call `resize(m_config.width, m_config.height);` on the view. This single call covers both modes:
  - Headed: resizes the visible QWidget window.
  - Headless (offscreen): QWebEngineView::resize() sets the off-screen surface size, so screenshots and PDF output use the configured viewport.
  The resize must happen BEFORE `load(QUrl("about:blank"))` so the initial render (and any subsequent `Page.captureScreenshot`) uses the correct dimensions.
  The call site should be just before or just after `show()` (which is only called in headed mode), but the resize itself is unconditional — apply it in both branches.

Acceptance criteria:
- In headed mode: the visible window opens at the configured width×height (default 1280×720, overridable via CLI)
- In headless mode: a `Page.captureScreenshot` CDP command returns an image whose pixel dimensions match the configured width×height
- `--width 800 --height 600` changes the viewport in both modes
- No regression in existing headed/headless startup behavior

tasks.title: Phase 3 – Validation: verify resolution flags end-to-end and document findings
tasks.description:
Manually validate the resolution feature end-to-end and record all findings in AGENTS.md and .jonggrang/progress.txt.

Validation steps:
1. Build: `cmake -B build && cmake --build build --parallel`
2. Headed default: `./build/anoa-browser --port 9223` — confirm window opens at 1280×720.
3. Headed override: `./build/anoa-browser --port 9223 --width 800 --height 600` — confirm window is 800×600.
4. Headless screenshot default: launch `./build/anoa-browser --headless --port 9224`, send CDP `Page.captureScreenshot` via websocket (use Node.js or wscat), decode base64 PNG, check image dimensions are 1280×720.
5. Headless screenshot override: launch with `--headless --width 1920 --height 1080`, repeat step 4, confirm 1920×1080.
6. Config file: write `{"width":640,"height":480}` to a JSON file, launch with `--config <file>`, verify dimensions are 640×480.
7. CLI override beats config file: launch with `--config <file> --width 1024`, verify width is 1024, height is 480 from file.
8. Invalid input: `--width 0` and `--width abc` — confirm exit code 1 with descriptive message.

Files to update:
- AGENTS.md: Add a row to the Protocol Gap Matrix (or a new "Resolution Feature" sub-section under Known Gotchas) documenting that `resize()` must precede `load()`. Note any discovered quirks (e.g. macOS vs Linux behavior, offscreen DPI).
- .jonggrang/progress.txt: Append a validation summary section with PASS/FAIL results for each step above.

Acceptance criteria:
- All 8 steps pass or failures are documented with workarounds
- AGENTS.md reflects any new gotchas found during validation
- .jonggrang/progress.txt contains a complete resolution-feature validation summary
